# Exact versions in every manifest, and bun is the only installer

> A range says *some* version and a lockfile pins it for one checkout only, so a fresh `cargo add` or a deleted lockfile resolves differently and the difference shows up as a failure nobody edited into existence.

Applies to `web/**`, `app/**`, `crates/**`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **Caret or tilde ranges, letting patches arrive on their own** (nothing refuses it) — A patch that lands without anyone choosing it is also a patch nobody tested. Upgrades should be a commit with a name on them.
- **npm alongside bun** (nothing refuses it) — They write different lockfiles from one manifest, and a repository carrying both has two answers to "what version is this".
- **Pinning the whole transitive graph by hand** (nothing refuses it) — Fiction. The lockfile owns transitive versions; the pin is on direct dependencies.

## What keeps it

Nothing can. The claim is about `package.json` and `Cargo.toml`, and archwarden reads source files rather than manifests. A rule shaped like this would be worth having; today the guard is review. Filed upstream as archwarden#177.
